_comment: Owner 24 Oct 2026 creature touches: 'adding some energy, some elemental effects, and some war torn appearance or hardened appearance to give the unique but still realistic look. Don't go overboard.' One or two light touches per species on the existing model, a small part of the body, realistic first; no red/oxblood. Baked into the remake's own albedo by tools/art_pipeline/creature_touch.py (overlays as in tools/creature_overlays.py, placed by the anatomy map: unit y = height, z = length with the head near 0.85-1.0, radial = distance from the body axis).

overlays._why: Hardened: a darker, mud-crusted shield of hide over the shoulders, the way a wallowing boar's shoulders cake and toughen.
War-torn: a pale scar line across the snout and cheek.

mudsnout._why_gpu_1024: GPU A+C (24 Oct): invisible at stage distance and 'a plain real-world boar'. Bolder hardened hide and scar, plus amber earth-glow seams cracking the shoulder hide (glow); the tusks are the nat1024t build.
mudsnout._why_close1024_b26: b26 (CPU, three judges): the amber seam shell read as gold glitter or an artefact on fur (-0.6 mapped), so the glow is off; the bolder weathering stays for b27.

overlays._why: Weathered (owner 25 Oct, one subtle unique touch): pale trail dust worked into the paws and lower legs of a coyote that lives on the roads. No scars: b26 judges read bolder scars as a seam.

cindercub._why: Owner 25 Oct: Cindercub needs definition and features. The near-black coat read as one value and the face was lost. A pale ash-grey mask on the muzzle, cheeks and brow gives the face and eyes a read; the ember cracks stay (embers are natural to fire).

overlays._why: Definition: a pale ash-grey muzzle, cheeks and brow, so the face and eyes read.
